Subject: Re: How will bundled context credits and minimums show up on EU invoices?

Thanks Olivia — good questions. Short answers up front, then a detailed sample mapping.

Short answers:
- We emit invoice lines by billing slab (route/model) and then an "apportionment" line for cross-slab sessions if a single call spans >1 slab.
- Discounts and monthly minimums apply at the account-commit level; usage above the minimum is billed net of discount. Credits (e.g., prefix cache amortization) are applied as a negative ledger line and pro-rated across invoice lines by usage weight.
- Rounding: generation tokens are billed per-started 512-token quantum for long-context routes (>16k). For chat routes (<4k) we use per-started 128-token quantum. Final invoice shows both raw token counts and rounded-charge quanta.

Detailed walkthrough (attached sample):
- Example session A (from your CSV): 18,450 total tokens generated across a single call that uses the long-context model. We split: 16,384 tokens in long slab + 2,066 overflow. Billing quanta: long slab charges = ceil(16384/512)=32 quanta; overflow charges = ceil(2066/512)=5 quanta. Total billed quanta = 37. Multiply by per-quanta price for long-context model, then apply the 20% commit discount at account level.

- Example session B (chat + embedding mix): small chat exchange 1,020 tokens (charged per-128 quantum -> ceil(1020/128)=8 quanta) plus an embedding call 3,200 embed-tokens (embedding priced per 1k vectors, shown as separate line). The invoice will include separate lines for chat and embeddings; the monthly minimum is compared to total net charge across all lines. If total net usage < monthly minimum, you'll see a top-up line to reach committed minimum.

- Credits: prefix/KV-cache credits (we agreed as part of the pilot) are computed daily and amortized by route weight. On the invoice you'll see a single negative "Cache amortization credit" with a short note containing the job id.

I attached a mocked EU invoice showing line-by-line math and a ledger apportionment page. Vanessa — can you confirm the rounding language and whether finance needs a different breakdown for their ledger system (e.g., separate lines per model version)?

Markus
VP, Strategic Accounts

Hi Olivia — attaching the sample ledger export (CSV tab) and a short illustrative invoice that uses three invoice lines: 
1) Chat (per-128 quantum)
2) Long-context generation (per-512 quantum)
3) Embeddings (per-1k units)

Two practical notes for your accounting team:
- We include both raw token columns and billed quanta columns. That gives you traceability back to raw usage and the rounded charge.
- For the EU VAT/region handling we keep the charge currency consistent (EUR) and show a single exchange-rate line if your contract was denominated in EUR but your contract originates in USD.

Sample invoice snippet (values simplified):
- Chat: raw tokens 1,020 -> 8 quanta @ €0.0025/quanta = €0.02
- Long-gen: raw tokens 18,450 -> 37 quanta @ €0.045/quanta = €1.665
- Embeddings: 3,200 units -> 3.2k units billed as 4 x 1k @ €0.015/1k = €0.06
Subtotal = €1.745 -> Commit discount 20% = -€0.349 -> Net = €1.396 -> Cache amortization credit = -€0.10 -> Invoice total = €1.296 (compare to monthly minimum €2.00 -> top-up = €0.704).

If Greenleaf prefers a different rounding quantum for long-gen (for example 256 tokens instead of 512) we can pilot that but it will shift per-quanta price because it changes unit economics.

Olivia / Paul — is the sample useful for your GL ledger team? If so I can produce a full 1-month export at day granularity for the pilot.

Thanks,
Vanessa
